en: to begin a class; to begin a course

examples.en: Universities start the semester in early March.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 영어 수업이 개강해서 바빠요.
examples.en: The English course starts next week, so I am busy.
The new class at the academy started on Monday.
I bought the textbook before the course started.

examples.ko: 방학이 끝나고 개강할 때가 되니 아쉬워요.
examples.en: Now that the break is over and school is about to start, I feel sad.
I heard the semester starts in the first week of September.

explain: 학교나 학원에서 새 학기나 새 강좌가 시작될 때 써요. 반대로 학기가 끝나는 것은 '종강하다'예요. 학생들은 '개강 첫날'처럼 명사로도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: There was a lot of homework from the first day of the semester.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사로 학기 시작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun form to talk about the start of a term.

phrases.en: When is the start date of classes?
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이 시작되는 날을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask when classes begin.

phrases.example: 친구들을 만날 수 있어서 개강을 기다려요.
phrases.en: I am looking forward to the semester because I can meet my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학기 시작을 기대할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking forward to a term starting.
phrases.en_equiv: to look forward to the start of class

explain_en: It is used when a new semester or course begins at a school or academy. The opposite, the end of a term, is '종강하다'. Students also use the noun form, as in '개강 첫날'.

examples.en: An economist appeared on the news and explained prices.
My uncle is an economist who works at a university.
Economists carefully predict next year's economy.
I want to become an economist someday.

examples.ko: 경제학자의 책을 읽고 돈에 대해 많이 배웠어요.
examples.en: I read an economist's book and learned a lot about money.
Each economist thinks differently about this opinion.

explain: '경제학자'는 경제를 연구하는 학자예요. 은행이나 회사에서 시장을 살피는 사람은 '이코노미스트'나 '분석가'라고 부르기도 해요. 뉴스에서 '유명 경제학자'처럼 이름 앞에 자주 붙어요.

phrases.en: A famous economist gave a lecture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 강연 소식에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in news and lecture announcements.

phrases.en: I want to become an economist when I grow up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about dreams or careers.

phrases.example: 경제학자의 말에 따르면 물가가 오를 거예요.
phrases.en: According to the economist, prices will rise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의 말에 따르면'은 전문가의 설명을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '의 말에 따르면' is used to report what an expert said.

explain_en: 경제학자 is a scholar who studies the economy. People who watch markets at banks or companies are sometimes called 이코노미스트 or 분석가. On the news you often see it before a name, as in 유명 경제학자.

examples.en: At Lunar New Year I go down to my hometown.
My grandmother still celebrates the Lunar New Year.
The highway is jammed during the Lunar New Year holiday.

examples.ko: 구정은 해마다 일월 말이나 이월에 있어요.
examples.en: Lunar New Year falls in late January or February each year.
When Lunar New Year comes, we eat tteokguk.
I got New Year's money at Lunar New Year.

explain: 음력 1월 1일을 부르던 옛 이름이에요. 지금은 공식 이름이 '설날'이고, 양력 1월 1일은 '신정'이에요. 어른들은 아직 '구정'이라고 많이 부르지만 젊은 사람들은 '설'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: These days, we eat rice cake soup with family on Lunar New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구정'보다 지금 공식적으로 쓰는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official name used today, instead of '구정'.

phrases.en: All the relatives gather at Lunar New Year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '때'를 붙이면 그 기간쯤을 가리키는 말이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '때' refers to that period of time.

phrases.en: Sinjeong is January 1 on the solar calendar, and Gujeong is January 1 on the lunar calendar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구정'과 짝이 되는 말로, 양력 새해 첫날이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of '구정': New Year's Day on the solar calendar.

explain_en: It is the old name for the first day of the lunar calendar. The official name now is 설날, and January 1 on the regular calendar is 신정. Older people still often say 구정, while younger people say 설.

examples.en: The presidential press corps gathered at the briefing room.
The manager shared his thoughts in front of the press corps.
I applied to the school newspaper's reporter team.

examples.ko: 현장을 취재하려고 기자단은 아침 일찍 출발했어요.
examples.en: The press group left early in the morning to cover the scene.

examples.ko: 청소년 기자단 활동을 하면서 글쓰기를 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned writing through youth reporter activities.
This company recruits a blogger reporter team.

explain: '기자단'은 정부나 기관을 함께 취재하는 기자들의 모임이에요. 학교나 회사에서는 글을 쓰며 알리는 학생이나 시민 모임도 '기자단'이라고 불러요. '기자들'은 그냥 여러 명이고 '기자단'은 하나의 조직이라는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: I joined the school press group.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임의 한 사람이 된다는 뜻으로 '가입하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '가입하다' to mean becoming a member of the group.

phrases.en: The mayor meets the press corps this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기자들이 모인 조직과 만나 이야기한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means meeting and talking with the organized group of reporters.

phrases.en: The student reporters write the school news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학생들이 모여 글을 쓰며 알리는 모임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a group of students who write and report news.

explain_en: 기자단 is a group of reporters who cover a government or organization together. Schools and companies also call a group of students or citizens who write and publicize things a 기자단. 기자들 just means several reporters, while 기자단 is one organization.

en: to act silly; to fool around

examples.en: My little brother keeps fooling around and it's chaotic.
You must not act silly in front of the teacher.
I was fooling around too much and broke a cup.
Stop messing around and sit quietly!

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 산책할 때 제일 많이 까불어요.
examples.en: My puppy acts the silliest when we go for walks.

examples.ko: 형이 아직도 애처럼 까부는 게 웃겨요.
examples.en: It's funny that my brother still acts like a kid.

explain: 까불다는 가볍고 시끄럽게 장난치는 모습이에요. 아이나 강아지에게는 귀엽게 들리지만 어른에게 '까불지 마'라고 하면 건방지다는 경고라서 아주 세게 들려요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '까부는, 까부세요'처럼 활용해요.

phrases.en: The classroom is noisy because of the kids fooling around.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㄹ이 빠진 활용형으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form with ㄹ dropped, modifying the noun after it.

phrases.en: Please don't fool around here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하라고 말할 때 써요. 반말 '까불지 마'는 아주 세게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tells someone to stop. The casual 까불지 마 sounds very harsh.

phrases.en: Stop fooling around and sit down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이어서 다음에 할 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -고 to link to what to do next.

explain_en: 까불다 describes noisy, light-hearted messing around. It sounds cute for a child or puppy, but telling an adult 까불지 마 is a harsh warning meaning "don't get cocky." The ㄹ drops before some endings, as in 까부는 and 까부세요.

examples.en: The baby is eating happily, yum-yum.
Yum-yum, this cake is really delicious!
The puppy is munching on its treat.

examples.ko: 우리 딸은 냠냠 소리를 내면서 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: My daughter makes yum-yum sounds while eating.
After eating it all up, I'm full.

examples.ko: 자, 이제 우리 같이 냠냠 해 볼까요?
examples.en: Now, shall we dig in together?

explain: 아이에게 '냠냠 먹자'처럼 말하거나 동화, 아기 말투에서 써요. 어른끼리 진지한 자리에서는 잘 안 써요. '쩝쩝'은 입 소리가 시끄럽다는 느낌이라 칭찬이 아니에요.

phrases.en: I said "Let's eat yum-yum!" to the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이에게 같이 먹자고 할 때 쓰는 귀여운 반말 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute casual-speech way to invite a child to eat together.

phrases.en: The child eats bread happily, yum-yum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛있게 먹는 소리와 모습을 함께 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows both the sound and the look of eating happily.

phrases.en: I eat slowly and enjoy my food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '냠냠'을 쓰지 않는 어른끼리의 말로, 어디서나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral version without '냠냠' that works for adults anywhere.
phrases.en_equiv: to eat well, enjoy a meal

explain_en: It is used when talking to children ('냠냠 먹자'), in picture books and baby talk, but rarely between adults in a serious setting. 쩝쩝 is a smacking noise and is not a compliment.

examples.ko: 병원에서 엑스레이를 찍으면 방사선이 아주 조금 나와요.
examples.en: When you take an X-ray at the hospital, a very small amount of radiation is emitted.

examples.ko: 방사선 치료를 받는 환자들이 이쪽에서 기다려요.
examples.en: Patients receiving radiation therapy wait over here.

examples.ko: 방사선을 막기 위해 납 옷을 입어요.
examples.en: They wear lead clothing to block radiation.

examples.ko: 우주 비행사는 강한 방사선에 노출될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Astronauts can be exposed to strong radiation.

examples.ko: 사고 뒤에 방사선 수치를 계속 확인하고 있어요.
examples.en: After the accident, they keep checking the radiation levels.

examples.ko: 방사선은 눈에 보이지 않아서 더 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Radiation can't be seen, so you have to be more careful.

explain: 병원, 원자력, 우주 이야기에서 나와요. 비슷한 '방사능'은 방사선을 내는 능력이나 물질을 가리켜서 뉴스에서 '방사능 유출'이라고 해요. 방사선은 나오는 빛이나 입자 자체예요.

phrases.example: 할머니는 병원에서 방사선 치료를 받고 계세요.
phrases.en: My grandmother is receiving radiation treatment at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 방사선으로 병을 치료하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to treating disease with radiation at a hospital.

phrases.en: The radiation exam is over in a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 엑스레이 같은 검사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for exams such as X-rays.

phrases.en: This machine gives off radiation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 물질에서 방사선이 밖으로 나온다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means radiation comes out of a machine or substance.

explain_en: It appears in talk about hospitals, nuclear power, and space. The similar 방사능 refers to the ability or material that gives off radiation, as in the news phrase '방사능 유출' (radioactive leak). 방사선 is the emitted rays or particles themselves.

examples.en: My grandfather has trouble walking.

examples.ko: 이 길은 보행 전용이라서 차가 못 들어와요.
examples.en: This road is for pedestrians only, so cars can't enter.
Looking at your phone while walking is dangerous.

examples.ko: 무릎을 다쳐서 보행 연습을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I hurt my knee, so I'm practicing walking.
Pedestrians must follow the signal.
Wait until the walk signal changes.

explain: '걷기'와 비슷하지만 안내문, 교통, 의료처럼 딱딱한 자리에서 써요. '보행자'(걷는 사람), '보행 신호'처럼 합쳐서 자주 나와요. 운동으로 걷는 건 '걷기'나 '산책'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Pedestrians must follow the traffic signal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 걷는 사람을 말하고 교통 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person walking on the road; common in traffic contexts.

phrases.en: Cross when the pedestrian signal turns green.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 길을 건너는 신호를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The signal that tells people when to cross the road.

phrases.en: Please don't look at your phone while walking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 '걷는 동안'을 짧게 쓸 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on signs as a short way of saying 'while walking'.

explain_en: It is close to 걷기 but belongs in formal settings such as signage, traffic, and medicine. It shows up in 보행자 (pedestrian) and 보행 신호 (walk signal). Walking for exercise is called 걷기 or 산책.

examples.en: The cold wind blew and I shivered.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 그가 부르르 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: Hearing that, he suddenly flared up in anger.
My phone buzzed, so I opened my bag.
The water for the ramen is bubbling up.

examples.ko: 아이가 차가운 물에 닿자 부르르 몸을 떨었어요.
examples.en: The child touched cold water and gave a shiver.
I suddenly got goosebumps and shuddered.

explain: 몸이 짧게 한 번 떨리거나 물건이 진동하는 모양, 물이 확 끓는 모양, 갑자기 성을 내는 모양에 써요. '부들부들'은 계속 떨리는 느낌이고 '부르르'는 짧고 갑작스러운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I got into the cold water and shuddered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧게 한 번 떠는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 계속 떠는 '부들부들'과 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a short, single shudder, unlike the continuous shaking of 부들부들.

phrases.en: The water is boiling up fast in the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 갑자기 확 끓어오르는 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes water suddenly coming to a rolling boil.

phrases.en: My phone vibrated during the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰 진동처럼 물건이 짧게 떨리는 소리와 모양에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an object, like a phone on vibrate, shaking briefly.

explain_en: It covers a quick shiver of the body, something vibrating, water suddenly boiling up, and a sudden flare of temper. '부들부들' feels like trembling that keeps going, while '부르르' is short and sudden.

examples.en: My stomach hurts often, so I booked an appointment at the gynecology department.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 부인과와 내과가 같이 있어요.
examples.en: This hospital has both gynecology and internal medicine.
Which floor is the gynecology department on?
My older sister went to get a gynecological checkup.

examples.ko: 부인과 의사 선생님이 친절하게 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: The gynecologist explained everything kindly.

examples.ko: 부인과 쪽 병원은 아침부터 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Gynecology clinics are crowded from the morning.

explain: 보통은 '산부인과'라고 말하고, '부인과'만 따로 쓰는 일은 적어서 병원 안내판이나 진료과 이름에서 볼 수 있어요. 임신과 출산은 '산과', 여성 몸의 질환은 '부인과'로 나눠요.

phrases.en: I came to get a gynecology checkup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 진료를 받는다고 말할 때 써요. '받다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at the hospital to say you're getting treatment. Used with 받다.

phrases.example: 일 년에 한 번 부인과 검진을 받아요.
phrases.en: I get a gynecological exam once a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 없는지 살펴보는 검사를 말해요. 건강검진 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A checkup to make sure nothing is wrong. Often comes up in talk about health exams.

phrases.example: 산부인과는 이 건물 삼 층에 있어요.
phrases.en: The OB-GYN is on the third floor of this building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실생활에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 임신과 출산도 함께 보는 병원이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word people use more in daily life. It also covers pregnancy and childbirth.

explain_en: People usually say 산부인과, and 부인과 alone mostly appears on hospital signs and department names. 산과 covers pregnancy and childbirth, while 부인과 covers women's health conditions.

en: to be outraged; to be infuriated

examples.en: Citizens were outraged by the unfair decision.
People get furious when they hear the news.
It's hard to calm an angry heart.
The furious customer shouted.
If you get too angry, your words become rough.
It's nothing to be furious about, so why are you like this?

explain: '화나다'보다 크고 무거운 감정이에요. 사회 문제나 불공평한 일에 많이 써요. 가벼운 일에는 '화나다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 사람들은 그 소식에 큰 분노를 느꼈어요.
phrases.en: People felt great anger at that news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '분노'를 써서 큰 화를 느꼈다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '분노' to say people felt strong anger.

phrases.en: Angry citizens gathered in the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 바꿔 사람을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form describes people who are outraged.

phrases.en: I got angry because my friend forgot our plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분노하다'보다 가볍고 일상에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter than '분노하다' and used in daily life.

explain_en: A bigger, heavier feeling than '화나다'. It is often used for social issues or unfair events. For small matters, '화나다' sounds natural.

examples.en: The business failed, and overnight I was buried in debt.

examples.ko: 빚더미에서 벗어나려고 아르바이트를 세 개 해요.
examples.en: I work three part-time jobs to get out from under my debt.

examples.ko: 빚더미 위에 앉은 기분이라 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I feel like I'm sitting on a heap of debt, so I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 카드를 막 쓰다가 빚더미가 되고 말았어요.
examples.en: I spent recklessly on cards and ended up deep in debt.

examples.ko: 아버지가 보증을 서서 우리 가족은 빚더미를 떠안았어요.
examples.en: My father co-signed a loan, and our family took on a mountain of debt.

examples.ko: 빚더미 속에서도 포기하지 않고 가게를 다시 열었어요.
examples.en: Even under a mountain of debt, he didn't give up and reopened the shop.

explain: 더미는 쌓인 덩어리라서, 빚이 산처럼 크다는 느낌을 줘요. 보통 '빚더미에 앉다, 빚더미에 오르다, 빚더미에서 벗어나다'처럼 정해진 짝으로 써요.

phrases.en: I failed at investing and ended up buried in debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갚기 힘들 만큼 큰 빚을 지게 되었다는 굳은 표현이에요. 실제로 앉는다는 뜻이 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set expression meaning to end up with debt too big to repay easily. It does not mean actually sitting.

explain_en: '더미' means a pile, so it gives the feeling of debt as big as a mountain. It usually goes with set verbs like '빚더미에 앉다', '빚더미에 오르다' and '빚더미에서 벗어나다'.

en: beef leg bone; beef shank bone

examples.en: I boiled the beef leg bones all day long.
On cold days, I think of bone broth soup.
I bought a pound of beef leg bones at the market.

examples.ko: 사골은 핏물을 먼저 빼고 끓여야 해요.
examples.en: You have to remove the blood from the bones before boiling them.

examples.ko: 엄마가 사골 육수로 떡국을 끓여 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom made tteokguk with bone broth for me.

examples.ko: 사골 국물에 밥을 말아 먹으면 든든해요.
examples.en: Eating rice in bone broth is very filling.

explain: 보통 뼈 자체보다 '사골국', '사골 육수'처럼 오래 끓인 국물 이야기로 많이 말해요. 뽀얗고 진한 국물이 나오고, 떡국이나 국수의 육수로도 써요. 집에서는 오래 끓이는 음식이라 '사골을 고다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 저녁에 따뜻한 사골국을 한 그릇 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I had a bowl of warm beef bone soup for dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사골을 오래 끓인 국물 요리를 가리켜요. 뼈보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the soup made by boiling the bones for a long time. It is used more often than the word for the bone itself.

phrases.example: 떡국은 사골 육수로 끓이면 더 맛있어요.
phrases.en: Tteokguk tastes better when you make it with beef bone broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국이나 국수의 국물 재료로 쓴다는 점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you talk about the broth as a base for soups or noodles.

phrases.en: I boiled beef bones down at home over the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사골을 오래 끓여서 진한 국물을 낸다는 동사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb phrase meaning to boil the bones for a long time to get a rich broth.

explain_en: People usually talk about it as '사골국' or '사골 육수', the long-simmered broth, rather than the bone itself. The broth turns milky and rich, and is also used as a base for tteokguk or noodles. Since it takes long to cook, people say '사골을 고다' (to simmer bones down).

examples.en: This year's car exports have grown compared with last year.
Semiconductor export figures appear in the news every month.
Export value keeps falling, so I'm worried about the economy.

examples.ko: 이 회사의 수출액은 한 해에 백억 원이 넘어요.
examples.en: This company's exports exceed ten billion won a year.

examples.ko: 쌀 수출액은 다른 품목보다 훨씬 적어요.
examples.en: The value of rice exports is much smaller than other items.
I heard last month's export value hit a record high.

explain: 뉴스에서 '수출액이 늘다/줄다', '수출액이 증가하다/감소하다'와 함께 자주 나와요. 금액이 아니라 양을 말할 때는 '수출량'을 써요.

phrases.en: This year, rice export value has dropped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔린 돈의 크기가 작아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount sold decreases.

phrases.en: Exports have increased greatly this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat formal phrase often used in the news.

phrases.en: The government announced this month's export figures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 숫자를 공개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an organization releases the numbers.

explain_en: In the news it often appears with '수출액이 늘다/줄다' and '증가하다/감소하다'. When you mean quantity rather than money, use '수출량'.

examples.en: It stings when I put disinfectant on the wound.
I fell, and my knee keeps stinging.
After the breakup, my heart ached a lot.
The painful experience made me stronger.
My back is sore from sunburn.
My eyes stung, so tears came out.

explain: '쓰리다'는 '배가 쓰리다'처럼 속이 아플 때도 쓰지만, '쓰라리다'는 쓸리거나 데인 상처가 쓰리고 아린 느낌이에요. 마음에 쓰면 '쓰라린 패배'처럼 괴롭고 아픈 경험을 말해요. '쓰라린'으로 명사를 꾸미는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I learned a lot from the painful experience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 아팠던 일을 말할 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for experiences that hurt emotionally.

phrases.en: I put medicine on it, so it doesn't sting anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상처의 아픔이 나아졌을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the wound's sting has eased.

phrases.en: I'm hungry, so my stomach burns.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쓰라리다'보다 넓게 속이 아플 때도 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than '쓰라리다', also used for stomach pain.

explain_en: '쓰리다' can describe an upset stomach, as in '배가 쓰리다', but '쓰라리다' is the stinging, smarting feeling of a scraped or burned wound. For the mind, it means a painful experience, as in '쓰라린 패배'. It is often used before a noun as '쓰라린'.

en: to be worrying; to be a cause for concern

examples.ko: 내일 비가 많이 와서 홍수가 우려돼요.
examples.en: Heavy rain tomorrow raises concerns about flooding.
Voices worried that the economy might get worse grew louder.

examples.ko: 건강 문제가 우려되는 사람은 병원에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If you have health concerns, please see a doctor.
The doctor said side effects are a concern.
Slow down when you are worried about an accident.
I was worried prices would go up, but luckily they stayed the same.

explain: '걱정되다'는 일상에서 누구나 쓰고, '우려되다'는 뉴스, 보고서, 공식적인 말에서 쓰는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. '걱정'은 사람의 마음, '우려'는 앞으로 나쁜 일이 생길 가능성이라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: There is great concern about environmental pollution.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우려'를 명사로 써서 걱정의 크기를 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 우려 as a noun to talk about how big the concern is. Common in the news.

phrases.en: Experts are concerned about rising prices.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정하는 사람이 주어일 때 써요. '우려되다'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the worried person is the subject. It pairs with 우려되다.

phrases.en: I'm worried about the test result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '우려되다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation this is used much more than 우려되다.

explain_en: '걱정되다' is the everyday word; '우려되다' is stiffer and appears in news, reports and formal speech. '걱정' is a personal worry, while '우려' is about the possibility of something bad happening.

examples.ko: 올해는 윤년이라서 이월이 이십구 일까지 있어요.
examples.en: This is a leap year, so February has 29 days.

examples.ko: 윤년은 사 년에 한 번 돌아와요.
examples.en: A leap year comes around once every four years.

examples.ko: 저는 윤년에 태어나서 생일이 사 년마다 있어요.
examples.en: I was born in a leap year, so my birthday comes every four years.
Do you know when the next leap year is?
In a leap year, there are 366 days.

examples.ko: 달력을 보고 이번 해가 윤년인지 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the calendar to see whether this year is a leap year.

explain: 하루가 더 있는 해를 말해요. 반대는 평년이에요. '윤년'은 날이 더해지고 '윤달'은 달이 더해지는 점이 달라요.

phrases.example: 윤년은 삼백육십육 일이고 평년은 삼백육십오 일이에요.
phrases.en: A leap year has 366 days and a common year has 365 days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말과 같이 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when explaining together with its opposite.

phrases.en: I was born in a leap year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태어난 해를 말할 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used to talk about one's birth year.
phrases.en_equiv: to be born in a leap year

phrases.example: 이월 이십구 일이 있는 해가 윤년이에요.
phrases.en: A year with February 29 is a leap year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 해가 윤년이라고 말하는 기본 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic sentence for saying a year is a leap year.

explain_en: It is a year with an extra day, and the opposite is '평년'. '윤년' adds a day, whereas '윤달' adds a month.

examples.ko: 버스 정류장 전광판에 도착 시간이 나와요.
examples.en: The arrival time shows on the board at the bus stop.

examples.ko: 경기장 전광판을 보면 점수를 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the score on the stadium board.

examples.ko: 전광판이 고장 나서 아무것도 안 보여요.
examples.en: The display broke, so nothing is shown.

examples.ko: 길 건너 전광판에서 광고가 계속 나와요.
examples.en: Ads keep playing on the electronic board across the street.
I checked the subway display before boarding.

examples.ko: 전광판 글자가 너무 작아서 안 보였어요.
examples.en: The letters on the display were too small to see.

explain: 전구나 화면으로 글자와 숫자를 보여 주는 큰 판이에요. 정류장, 경기장, 도로에서 볼 수 있어요. 종이로 된 '게시판'이나 '간판'과는 달리 내용이 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 경기가 끝나자 전광판에 우리 팀 이름이 떴어요.
phrases.en: When the game ended, our team's name appeared on the scoreboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자나 숫자가 화면에 나타날 때 '뜨다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '뜨다' is used when text or numbers appear on a screen.
phrases.en_equiv: to show up on the board

phrases.example: 건물 위 전광판 광고가 눈에 띄어요.
phrases.en: The ad on the electronic board above the building stands out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 화면으로 보여 주는 광고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An ad shown on a large electronic screen.

phrases.example: 역에 열차 시간을 알려 주는 안내 전광판이 있어요.
phrases.en: The station has an information board that shows train times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이나 시간을 알려 주는 전광판을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An electronic board that gives directions or times.

explain_en: It is a large board that shows letters and numbers with lights or a screen, seen at bus stops, stadiums, and roads. Unlike a 게시판 (notice board) or 간판 (shop sign), what it displays changes.

en: all over; everywhere; all at once

examples.en: The rumor spread all over the school.

examples.ko: 비가 쫙 쏟아져서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: The rain poured down and my clothes got soaked.
I ripped the paper in one go and threw it away.

examples.ko: 가방 지퍼를 쫙 열고 우산을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: I zipped the bag open in one pull and took out an umbrella.

examples.ko: 선생님이 책상 위에 종이를 쫙 펼치셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher spread the papers out wide on the desk.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 하루 만에 쫙 유행했어요.
examples.en: That song became a hit everywhere in just a day.

explain: '쭉', '확'과 달리 무언가가 한 번에 넓게 퍼지거나 길게 갈라지는 모습을 흉내 내는 말이에요. 소문이 퍼질 때, 비가 쏟아질 때, 종이를 찢을 때처럼 구어체에서 자주 써요. 글에서는 거의 안 쓰고 말할 때 생동감을 줘요.

phrases.en: I spread a blanket all over the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 곳에 한 번에 펼쳐 놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when spreading something wide over a large area at once.

phrases.en: I was angry and ripped the paper in one go.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번에 길게 갈라지게 찢는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes tearing something in one long, quick rip.
phrases.en_equiv: to rip apart in one go

phrases.en: After exercising, I lost weight quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살이나 물처럼 무엇이 한꺼번에 많이 빠질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something, like weight or water, drops away a lot all at once.

explain_en: An imitative word for something spreading wide or tearing/pulling open in one motion. It is common in speech for rumors spreading, rain pouring, ripping paper. It is rare in writing and adds liveliness when speaking.

examples.ko: 춘분에는 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같아요.
examples.en: On the spring equinox, day and night are almost the same length.
This year the spring equinox is around March 20.
After the spring equinox, the days gradually get longer.
I looked for the spring equinox on the calendar.
They say farmers began preparing for farming around the spring equinox.
On the spring and autumn equinoxes, the sun rises due east.

explain: 24절기 중 하나로, 보통 3월 20일 전후예요. 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같고, 이후부터 낮이 길어져요. 짝이 되는 말은 가을의 '추분'이에요.

phrases.en: The spring equinox has passed, so the days have gotten longer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춘분 이후의 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about changes after the equinox.

phrases.en: Around the spring equinox, the weather starts to get warmer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 날짜 즈음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to mean around that date.

phrases.example: 춘분에는 낮과 밤의 길이가 거의 같아요.
phrases.en: On the spring equinox, day and night are almost the same length.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에는'을 붙여 그날의 특징을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에는, used to describe that day's features.

explain_en: It's one of the 24 solar terms, usually around March 20. Day and night are nearly equal, and the days get longer afterward. Its autumn counterpart is '추분'.

examples.ko: 저는 콩밥을 좋아해서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: I like rice with beans, so I often make it.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 콩밥이 싫어서 콩만 골라냈어요.
examples.en: As a child I hated bean rice and picked out only the beans.
Tonight's dinner is bean rice with doenjang stew.
They say rice with beans is good for your health.
I put beans in the rice and made bean rice.
Please give me one more bowl of bean rice.

explain: 쌀에 콩을 섞어 지은 밥이에요. 비슷하게 '잡곡밥', '보리밥'처럼 재료를 앞에 붙여 말해요. 아래 표현처럼 말이 달라지는 쓰임도 있어요.

phrases.example: 나쁜 짓을 하면 콩밥을 먹게 돼요.
phrases.en: If you do bad things, you'll end up in prison.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감옥에 간다는 뜻의 속된 표현이에요. 가볍게 농담처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slangy way to say someone goes to prison. It is used in a joking tone.

explain_en: It is rice cooked with beans mixed in. Similar words put the ingredient first, such as '잡곡밥' (multigrain rice) and '보리밥' (barley rice). It also has a figurative use shown below.

en: to be invested (money put in for profit)

examples.en: A lot of money is invested in this business.
Time was invested in studying.

examples.ko: 그 돈은 새 공장에 투자될 거예요.
examples.en: The money will be invested in a new factory.
The amount invested grows every year.
I'm worried because the money isn't being invested properly.
The money invested in the research isn't wasted.

explain: '투자되다'는 돈이나 시간, 노력이 어디에 쓰였는지 말할 때 써요. '~에 투자되다'로 쓰고, 투자하는 사람을 말하면 '투자하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: A lot of money is being invested in this business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속되는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something happening right now.

phrases.en: Not enough money is invested in education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부족하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that the amount is not enough.

phrases.en: I invest in stocks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투자하는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person investing is the subject.

explain_en: 투자되다 tells where money, time or effort has been put. It takes 에, as in '~에 투자되다'. When you name the person who invests, use 투자하다.

examples.en: New potatoes came out, so I steamed and ate them.
I bought a box of new potatoes at the market.
A stir-fry made with new potatoes is delicious.
New potatoes have thin skin, so they're easy to peel.
My mother sent me new potatoes.
New potatoes taste good with just a sprinkle of salt.

explain: '햇-'은 그해에 처음 나온 것 앞에 붙어서 햇과일, 햇고구마, 햅쌀처럼 써요. 햅쌀은 '햇쌀'이 아니라 '햅쌀'로 쓰니 주의하세요. 오래 두고 먹은 것은 '묵은 감자'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Braised new potatoes are soft and tasty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇감자로 만든 반찬 이름 앞에 붙여 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can put it before the name of a dish made with new potatoes.

phrases.en: I boiled new potatoes and ate them with salt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 방법을 말할 때 '삶다', '찌다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with cooking verbs like 삶다 and 찌다.

phrases.en: New potatoes come out around June.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올해 첫 수확이 시장에 나오는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for when the first harvest of the year reaches the market.

explain_en: '햇-' is put before things that came out for the first time that year, as in 햇과일, 햇고구마 and 햅쌀. Note that new rice is '햅쌀', not '햇쌀'. Potatoes kept for a long time are called '묵은 감자'.
